criteria.title: Every repository under the enabled roots appears exactly once

checks.assert: Over the whole corpus each fixture yields exactly one project row; linked worktrees resolve to their parent; bare repositories are detected.
submodule-child and submodule-nested are projects of their own with a submodule_edge row to the parent.
A bare fixture reports as bare at the project level.
checks.reason: project.is_bare is computed and never written: the column exists NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, two derivations produce the value, and create() hard-codes 0. Bareness is a property of a location and the column is on project, so whoever takes it must first rule on what a project with one bare and one non-bare copy reports.

criteria.title: Copies collapse, forks stay apart, ambiguous lineage is flagged

checks.assert: copy-one and copy-two on two volumes become one project with two locations.
fork and upstream remain two projects sharing a lineage_key with different remote_keys.
ambiguous-lineage becomes its own project with ambiguous_lineage set, and problems.list names both candidate lineages.
Amendment 2: projects.merge has zero call sites outside the test suite; a control wired to it is the §17 breach §11.1 forbids by name.

criteria.title: A merge is transactional and loses no work

checks.assert: Amendment 3: git-derived rows are deleted and recomputed for the survivor, session-derived rows are reparented, a redirect is written, level_floor cannot fall, and projects.merged is emitted.

criteria.title: Unplugging a volume freezes and deletes nothing; re-plugging restores

checks.assert: FakeMountResolver::unmount over vol-b moves those locations to offline, freezes condition, and every project, location, session and xp_events row is byte-identical before and after.
mount() plus a rescan returns the same location rows to present.

criteria.title: Hostile repositories index without crashing and contribute no wrong date

checks.assert: zero-commit, shallow, non-utf8-path, long-path, dubious-ownership and index-lock-held all reach a terminal job state with no panic.
future-dated raises clock_skew and contributes to no era boundary, no reveal figure and no commit-day.

criteria.title: Editing a tracked file and re-observing flips is:dirty to true

checks.assert: The v1 regression: a plain fs::write to a tracked file, with no git command in between, must flip is_dirty on the next J2. Prove it by re-introducing an index-mtime cache and watching this test fail.

checks.test: AC-6 is:dirty matches the edited project
checks.assert: The shelf query is:dirty selects that project after the re-observation.

criteria.title: Play, the dropdown, the overrides and the five resolution tiers

checks.assert: Amendment 7: project override, location override, language default, global default, ask — first hit wins, a tier with no row is skipped, primary_language NULL resolves at global, targets.list returns the tier that resolved, resolution never consults verify_state.
Re-detection rewrites exec_bytes for every row matching the re-detected (kind, name), language rows included; a fresh install ships no built-in language-to-editor table.

checks.test: AC-7 a stale target path is detected before spawn
checks.assert: targets.verify marks a removed executable missing and Play refuses before spawning.

criteria.title: A WSL-resident repository launches with translated paths

checks.assert: Windows-to-distro and distro-to-Windows translation round-trips for drive-mounted, VHD-resident and UNC paths.

checks.reason: No CI runner provides a WSL distro: nested virtualisation is not available on hosted Windows runners, so the in-distro worker cannot be started. Run on Reference A before a release. The bridge has never been crossed on a real machine here either — the dispatcher is asserted over a loopback worker only.
checks.assert: A repository inside a distro launches its target and runs git inside the distro.

criteria.title: The query grammar, its soft errors and saved queries

checks.test: AC-9 the grammar parses every documented field, negation and comparison
checks.assert: The query conformance corpus runs in both the renderer and the core and produces identical ASTs.

checks.test: AC-9 an unknown field soft-errors without discarding the query
checks.assert: The unknown term is dropped, named in the ignored clause, and the surviving terms still run.

checks.test: AC-9 a saved query survives a restart
checks.assert: A saved collection re-lights after a relaunch by AST comparison against the restored query.

criteria.title: Peek is plain text; view state restores exactly

checks.test: AC-10 Space peeks inline as plain text
checks.assert: Peek renders the README as literal text — no markup, no fetch, no navigation.

checks.test: AC-10 view state restores exactly across a relaunch
checks.assert: Amendment 10: query, sort, view mode (grid|list), density, collapsed sections, scroll offset, selection, dismissed notices and window geometry all restore.
checks.reason: No geometry restore exists: viewState always writes null for the window rectangle and nothing in the shell reads it. Whoever lands the restore must clamp to the measured top-bar floor in the same change, or a window narrowed once stays broken.

criteria.title: Sessions: wait mode, idle segmentation, isolation, orphan recovery

checks.assert: A wait-mode target closes its session with close_reason process_exit.
With FakeClock, a tree that never changed credits at most 20 minutes to a segment.
Shelf interaction does not extend an open segment belonging to a different project.
A session with no ended_at from a previous process closes with close_reason orphaned.

criteria.title: First run asks nothing, shows no percentage, states its coverage

checks.test: AC-12 first run asks nothing, shows no percentage, and states its coverage
checks.assert: The first-run flow presents no configuration input and no percentage anywhere, and the word setup appears in no rendered string. Asserted over the mounted gate in jsdom, which has no layout engine — the same clause against a real frame is AC-12-paints.

checks.test: AC-12 the first-run screen paints and the word setup is absent from it
checks.assert: The same clause against a composited frame rather than a jsdom tree.
checks.reason: The e2e that renders the first-run screen skips itself when core/target/release/codotheca-core is absent — honestly, rather than passing over a blank window — so on any machine or CI job that has not built a release core the check does not run at all. Making it automated would mark a criterion covered by a test that silently declines to execute.

checks.test: AC-12 every figure over a partial index states its coverage
checks.assert: Every reveal figure carries its RevealBasis coverage line, with shallow repositories excluded from the maths and counted in the coverage line.

checks.test: AC-12 a refused suggestion says why rather than nothing
checks.assert: §10.1a requires an explanation and never a silent no.
checks.reason: The shell distinguishes an unknown suggestion from an ambiguous one and the renderer collapses both to no root added: the commit path returns a root-add reply and the refusal type has no variant for it. What a user sees today is a scan that found nothing under a root nobody added. Closing it is a schema change plus 16b's surface.

criteria.title: Two launches: the second focuses the first and starts no second core

checks.test: AC-13 a second launch opens no window and starts no core
checks.assert: With one instance running, a second process exits without opening a window and without taking the core lock.
checks.reason: Plan 20's File Structure names app/e2e/acceptance_single_instance.spec.ts and no task in plan 20 or 20b creates it; the single-instance lock itself is the shell plan's code. Registering it automated against a spec nobody wrote would be a criterion marked covered by a test that does not exist.
Focus transfer to an existing window is not observable under xvfb: there is no window manager, so focus semantics on a headless runner are unrepresentative of either target.
checks.assert: The second launch raises and focuses the first window.

criteria.title: A future schema refuses to open; a corrupt database quarantines and rebuilds

checks.assert: A PRAGMA user_version above SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION yields SchemaFromFuture carrying both numbers, and the file is left untouched.
A corrupt file is quarantined with its wal and shm, rebuild returns a RebuildReport, and the report names exactly what was not derivable.

checks.test: AC-14 the failure window states the schema number and the restore time
checks.assert: Criterion 57's failed-migration window renders the restored schema number and the restore time.

criteria.title: Cold launch to first painted tiles

checks.assert: p50 under 800 ms and p95 under 1.5 s on A; p95 under 2.5 s on B. Chromium bootstrap dominates and v1's 300 ms was not achievable.
checks.reason: The terminal event now exists and has been observed: an end-to-end spec launches the real app and asserts a real pixel against a blank frame of the same window. Nothing times it. No harness records the pair below, no run has produced a p50 or a p95, and the spec that proves the paint skips itself when core/target/release/codotheca-core is absent. What is true today is that the app paints; what this budget claims is unmeasured.

criteria.title: Resident hotkey to window visible

checks.assert: Window alive: p95 under 30 ms. Measured 9 ms p50 / 12.6 ms p95. Amendment 16: the harness binds a chord first, because the resident shortcut ships unbound.

measurement.to: a composited frame of the window
measurement.state: window alive, chord bound by the harness

checks.assert: Window destroyed: p95 under 250 ms. Measured 134 ms p50 / 150 ms p95.

measurement.to: a composited frame of the recreated window

criteria.title: Keystroke to refiltered grid at 1,000 projects

checks.assert: p95 under 16 ms over a named query corpus, measured through to presentation. p99 was dropped in v2.1 because no harness can produce it honestly.

criteria.title: Cache-validation pass over 1,000 repositories

checks.assert: Under 5 s with every fingerprint unchanged and no J2 re-run. This is what v1's full T2 refresh under 5 s actually described.

measurement.state: 1,000 repositories, all fingerprints unchanged, no J2 re-run

criteria.title: Forced J2 and J3 refresh over 1,000 repositories

checks.assert: 75 to 120 s, reported with the Reference split, since deprioritising Reference repositories removes about 61% of the work from the critical path. Measured 584 ms per repository excluding the worst outlier.

measurement.state: 1,000 repositories on local SSD, freshness reset, fully backgrounded

checks.assert: The UI never blocks during the refresh: frame pacing during the run holds criterion 30's rate.

measurement.run: wheel-driven scrolling through the shelf for at least 450 frames while the forced refresh runs

criteria.title: First full J4 history index over 1,000 repositories

checks.assert: J4 stopped mid-run resumes from project_job_state.cursor and produces the same commit-day set as an uninterrupted run.
checks.reason: §4.1's chunking is unreachable today and accepted for phase 1: the git backend exposes atomic calls with no yield point, so there is nowhere to write a cursor. The contract is built — a partial outcome, its application and the cursor column all exist — so closing it is additive. Overturn on measurement, not taste.

checks.test: AC-20 the coverage indicator is visible while J4 is incomplete
checks.assert: A week outside J4's coverage is not computed, and the panel carries its coverage line.

checks.reason: The criterion states no deadline — 'minutes, resumable, with a visible coverage indicator. No deadline.' There is nothing to gate on, and a ceiling invented here would gate on a number the spec deliberately declined to state.
checks.assert: No duration budget exists for the first full J4 pass.

checks.reason: The corpus tops out at the deep-history fixture, which reached 2,585 commits. About 30 ms fixed plus 0.02 ms per commit implies roughly 2 s at 100k commits and 20 s at 1M, but that is an extrapolation from a fit, not a measurement, and the harness records extrapolations as extrapolations.
checks.assert: The 100k and 1M commit cases are extrapolated and are never reported as measured.

criteria.title: Idle on Reference A

checks.assert: Amendment 21: zero scheduled frames while unfocused or hidden, and at most one flicker element while focused, sampled over at least 60 s in the defined idle state.

measurement.run: at least 60 s with the shelf visible and focused, no project page open, no session open, no job running, and no pointer or keyboard input for at least 5 s

checks.test: AC-21 the scheduled flicker obeys its eligibility and its parameters
checks.assert: At most one card in the viewport — mounted is not enough; 1 to 2 sub-dips of 15 to 25% of steady glow, each 80 to 140 ms, a deterministic Poisson process at about 9 s mean seeded per session, suspended while unfocused and resuming with no backlog. Eligibility is condition_signal in {neglected, abandoned}, location present, is_reference = 0. The design's 50% depth, fixed 130 ms hold and fixed 9,000 ms period are cut and must not be asserted.

checks.reason: Amendment 21 marks the CPU figure provisional: the 0.014 to 0.017% in the probe results was taken before any scheduled frame existed, so it describes a different build. It is re-measured before the public beta rather than gated on now.
checks.assert: No idle CPU or GPU budget is gated in phase 1.

checks.reason: Asserting the app is absent from the OS audio mixer requires an OS audio mixer; no hosted CI runner exposes one, and a stubbed audio device would assert the stub.
checks.assert: The app does not appear in the OS audio mixer while idle.

criteria.title: Storage against the 1,000-project fixture

checks.assert: Main database plus WAL under 100 MB against the fixture of 1,000 projects, 200,000 commit subjects and 100,000 events.
checks.reason: The file exists and holds the art half only. The other half was deliberately not stubbed, because a stub reports passed for a budget nothing measured, and the 1,000-project fixture belongs to the jobs plan and to no other. The file is shared; the owner is per-function.

checks.assert: Art cache under 50 MB against the re-derived total, with the card rendition asserted at 600x900 and the hero cache bounded, least-recently-opened evicted first. The GPU texture clause is phase 3 and is not tested. The 1,000-project total is projected from the worst of a 24-scene sample rather than rasterized in full, which the test states; the eviction order is observed over more opens than the cap.

measurement.state: the worst of a 24-scene sample projected to 1,000 projects, with more hero opens than the cap

criteria.title: Scroll frame pacing

checks.assert: At most 1% of frames miss a display refresh over a run of at least 450 frames, at whatever interval the display actually reports. This criterion carries a run definition and no event pair, because it gates a rate. Measured DOM-only on A: 0 of 450 missed.

measurement.run: 1,000 logical cards with 140 mounted, virtualized, driven by injected wheel events through the real compositor path and never by assigning scrollTop, over at least 450 frames, with the window alive, the shelf already painted and the virtualizer settled

criteria.title: Palette painted with its first page of rows

checks.assert: In-app palette chord with the window alive: p95 under 50 ms. A budget, not a measurement, and it must be measured before the bar is claimed.

measurement.to: the palette painted with its first page of rows and the field focused

checks.assert: The resident show shortcut with the window destroyed: p95 under 300 ms, against a chord the harness binds. This is the same press criterion 16 measures; 16's terminal event precedes 31's inside it.

measurement.to: the palette painted with its first page of rows and the field focused
measurement.state: window destroyed, chord bound by the harness
